text: Komodo dragons are the biggest lizards in the world. They use their forked tongues to smell the air.
A bearded dragon can puff out the spiky skin under its chin. It looks like a beard, and that is how it got its name.
Dragonflies have huge eyes. They can see in almost every direction at once.
A dragonfly can fly forward and backward. It can even stay still in one spot, like a tiny helicopter.
Leafy sea dragons are fish that look like floating seaweed. Their leafy fins help them hide in the ocean.
In a sea dragon family, the dad carries the eggs on the underside of his tail until they hatch.
Some small lizards called flying dragons can glide from tree to tree. They spread flaps of skin like wings.
A chameleon can move each eye on its own. It can look in two different ways at the same time.
Geckos can walk up walls and even across ceilings. Tiny hairs on their toes help them stick.

source.name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Explorers: Gecko

text: Many lizards shed their old skin as they grow. A fresh new skin is waiting underneath.
Komodo dragons live on hot, dry islands. They like to rest in the shade when the Sun gets too warm.
A bearded dragon can make its beard turn dark. A dark beard can mean it is alarmed or wants to look tough.
Dragonflies have four long wings. When they rest, most dragonflies hold their wings out flat, like an airplane.
The Komodo dragon lives on a few islands in Indonesia. It can grow to about ten feet long and is the largest lizard alive today.
Komodo dragons can hear, but not very well. Their forked tongue is their best tool, picking up smells from far away.
Bearded dragons come from the dry lands of Australia. They sometimes wave one front leg slowly, which scientists think is a signal to other bearded dragons.
Dragonflies begin life underwater as young insects. When they are ready, they climb up a plant stem and come out with wings.

source.name: Iowa DNR: 6 cool things about dragonflies

text: Dragonflies have four wings that can each move on their own. This lets them turn quickly, stop in midair, and even fly backward.

source.name: Iowa DNR: 6 cool things about dragonflies

text: Leafy sea dragons live only in the cool waters off southern and western Australia. They drift slowly and sway like seaweed, so few animals ever notice them.
Flying dragon lizards live in the forests of Southeast Asia. They open flaps of skin held out by long ribs and glide from one tree to another.
Chameleons change color to show how they feel and to warm up or cool down.
Geckos are among the few lizards that can make sounds. Some squeak, click, or bark softly to talk to each other.

source.name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Explorers: Gecko

text: The marine iguana of the Galapagos Islands is the only lizard that swims in the sea to find its food. It munches on seaweed growing on underwater rocks.
The frilled lizard of Australia opens a big, colorful frill around its neck when it feels threatened. The frill helps keep other animals away.
The Chinese water dragon is a lizard that loves water. It is a strong swimmer and can stay underwater for many minutes by holding its breath.

source.name: Smithsonian National Zoo: Asian water dragon

text: A giraffe has a long, dark tongue. It uses its tongue to reach leaves high up in tall trees.
Elephants use their trunks to drink, to smell, to pick things up, and to greet their friends.
A hummingbird flaps its wings so fast that they make a humming sound. That is how it got its name.
Honeybees do a little dance to tell other bees where to find flowers full of food.

source.name: Smithsonian: What is the Waggle Dance

text: Penguins cannot fly, but they are great swimmers. Their wings work like flippers in the water.
An owl can turn its head about three quarters of the way around to look behind it.
Cats spend a big part of each day sleeping. Some cats sleep for more than half the day.

source.name: Britannica: Why do cats sleep so much

text: A baby kangaroo is called a joey. It rides in a warm pouch on its mother.
Butterflies can taste with their feet. A mother butterfly stands on a leaf to find out if it is a good plant for her eggs.
Sloths move so slowly that tiny green plants called algae can grow on their fur.

source.name: Smithsonian National Zoo: Why are sloths so slow

text: A snail carries its home on its back. When it feels unsafe, it pulls itself inside its shell.
Polar bears have black skin under their white fur. Thick fur and a layer of fat keep them warm in the snow.

source.name: Britannica: Why are polar bears white

text: Some parrots can learn to copy many words and sounds.
A group of flamingos is often called a flamboyance. Flamingos get their pink color from the tiny shrimp and algae they eat.

source.name: Smithsonian National Zoo: Why are flamingos pink

text: Arctic terns fly from the far north of the world to the far south and back again every year. That is one of the longest trips any animal makes.
Elephants make low rumbling sounds to talk to each other. Some of these sounds are so deep that people cannot hear them.
To make honey, honeybees must visit a very large number of flowers. They carry the sweet nectar back to the hive.
Owls can fly almost silently. Soft edges on their feathers help their wings stay quiet as they glide through the night.
Hummingbirds can hover in one spot and even fly backward. Their wings move in the shape of a figure eight.
A cheetah is the fastest land animal. In a short sprint, it can run about as fast as a car on a highway.
Some ants can carry things many times heavier than their own bodies. They often work as a team to move big loads.
Koalas spend most of the day asleep, often more than eighteen hours. The leaves they eat give them very little energy.
Each zebra has its own pattern of stripes, much like a fingerprint. No two zebras have exactly the same stripes.
Crows are very clever birds. They can remember the faces of people they have met.

source.name: Cornell Lab All About Birds: Remember me? Crows do

text: The platypus is a mammal that lays eggs. It has a bill like a duck and finds its food underwater with its eyes closed.
The Sun is a star. It looks so big because it is much closer to us than any other star.

source.name: NASA Space Place: All About the Sun

text: The Moon has no air and no wind. Footprints left by astronauts can stay there for a very long time.

source.name: NASA Space Place: All About the Moon

text: Saturn has big, bright rings. They are made of chunks of ice and rock.
Jupiter is the biggest planet in our solar system. More than a thousand Earths could fit inside it.
Mars looks red because its dirt has rust in it. People call it the Red Planet.
Astronauts on the space station see the Sun rise and set many times every day.

source.name: NASA: Year in Space crew sunrises and sunsets

text: In space there is no air, so there is no sound. Astronauts use radios to talk to each other.

source.name: NASA Space Place: How Scary Is Space

text: The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight bounces off it.

source.name: NASA Space Place: All About the Moon

text: Venus is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun. Its thick air holds in the heat like a blanket.

source.name: NASA Space Place: All About Venus

text: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus, because the planet spins very slowly as it goes around the Sun.

source.name: NASA Space Place: All About Venus

text: Scientists think there are more stars in space than grains of sand on all the beaches on Earth.

source.name: ESA: More stars than grains of sand on Earth

text: Shooting stars are not really stars. They are tiny bits of space rock glowing as they zip through the air.

source.name: NASA Science: Meteors and meteorites facts

text: The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth. It drifts a tiny bit farther each year.

source.name: NASA StarChild: Did you know the Moon

text: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the solar system. It is much taller than Mount Everest.
Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth. When you see the Sun, you are seeing light that left it eight minutes ago.
Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system. They blow faster than the speed of sound on Earth.
Astronauts on the space station float because they are falling around the Earth all the time. They move so fast that they keep missing the ground.
Saturn is so light for its size that it would float in water, if there were a bathtub big enough to hold it.
Neptune is so far from the Sun that one trip around it takes about a hundred and sixty five Earth years.
A neutron star is so tightly packed that a single spoonful of it would weigh about as much as a mountain.

source.name: NASA Imagine the Universe: Neutron stars

text: The Milky Way is our home galaxy. On a dark night far from city lights, it looks like a faint, glowing band across the sky.

source.name: NASA Imagine the Universe: Milky Way

text: Mercury has almost no air to hold in heat. Its days are scorching hot, and its nights are freezing cold.

source.name: NASA Space Place: All About Mercury

text: Jupiter has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot. The storm is wider than the whole Earth and has been swirling for hundreds of years.

source.name: NASA Science: Tour of storms across the solar system

text: A year on Mercury lasts only about three Earth months. It races around the Sun on the shortest path of any planet.

source.name: NASA Space Place: All About Mercury

text: Mars has giant dust storms. Some grow so large that they wrap all the way around the planet.

source.name: NASA Science: Tour of storms across the solar system

text: Lava is melted rock. When it cools down, it turns hard and becomes new rock.

source.name: USGS: What is the difference between magma and lava?

text: Some volcanoes are under the sea. When they grow tall enough, they can make new islands.

source.name: NOAA Ocean Exploration: How seamounts form

text: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above the sea. It is so high that the air up there is thin and cold.
Diamonds are made of the same stuff as pencil lead. It is called carbon.
Some caves have stone shapes hanging from the ceiling like icicles. They grow drip by drip.

source.name: NOAA: Difference between a stalactite and a stalagmite

text: The center of the Earth is very hot. It is about as hot as the surface of the Sun.

source.name: Smithsonian Magazine: Center of the Earth is as hot as the Sun

text: A rock called pumice is so full of tiny air holes that it can float on water.
A geyser is a hot spring that shoots water and steam high into the air.
Sand on many beaches is made of tiny bits of rock and shell, worn down by the waves.
Most of the Earth is covered by water. That is why it looks blue from space.
Salt is a crystal. If you look very closely, each grain of salt is a tiny cube.
Some lakes are so salty that people can float on top of the water with no effort.

source.name: Wonderopolis: Is the Dead Sea deadly?

text: Glaciers are huge rivers of ice. They move very, very slowly across the land.

source.name: NASA Climate Kids: 10 things about glaciers

text: Volcanic ash makes soil very rich. That is why farmers often grow crops on the slopes of old volcanoes.

source.name: British Geological Survey: Living with volcanoes

text: The islands of Hawaii were made by volcanoes rising from the sea floor. Some of those volcanoes are still adding new land today.
Obsidian is a shiny black glass made when lava cools very quickly. It cools so fast that crystals do not have time to form.
Mount Everest grows a tiny bit taller each year. Huge plates of rock under the ground slowly push together, and that helps lift it up.

source.name: Smithsonian Magazine: Why Mount Everest grows taller each year

text: The Earth is made of layers, a bit like a peach: a thin crust, a thick mantle, and a metal core in the middle.
Geodes look like plain round rocks on the outside. When they are cracked open, many are lined with sparkling crystals.
Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth. A desert is any place that gets very little rain or snow, even if it is freezing cold.

source.name: Live Science: Largest desert on Earth

text: Quartz is one of the most common minerals in the crust of the Earth. Much of the sand on beaches is made of tiny grains of quartz.
Yellowstone National Park has about half of all the geysers in the world. Its most famous geyser, Old Faithful, erupts many times each day.

source.name: NPS Yellowstone: Old Faithful treasures, geysers

text: The Earth acts like a giant magnet. That is why the needle of a compass points north.

source.name: Wonderopolis: How does a compass work?

text: Iceland sits on a crack between two huge plates of rock. That is why it has so many volcanoes and hot springs.
Rubies and sapphires are the same mineral, called corundum. Tiny amounts of other metals make rubies red and sapphires blue.
A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through raindrops. The light splits into many colors.

source.name: Met Office: How are rainbows formed?

text: Most snowflakes have six sides or six arms. Each one is made of tiny ice crystals.
Clouds are made of tiny drops of water or bits of ice floating in the air.

source.name: NASA GPM: What are clouds made of?

text: A flash of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Thunder is the sound that lightning makes. Light travels faster than sound, so we see the flash first.
Fog is a cloud that sits low, right down near the ground.
Hail is made of balls of ice that fall from big storm clouds.
Wind is moving air. The Sun warms some places more than others, and that makes the air move.
On cold nights, water in the air can freeze onto grass and windows. This sparkly ice is called frost.
On cool mornings, little drops of water called dew can appear on grass and spider webs.
Snow looks white, but each snowflake is made of clear ice.

source.name: Live Science: Why is snow white?

text: A weather vane turns in the breeze. Its arrow points to where the wind is coming from.
Puddles dry up because the Sun warms the water. The water turns into a gas and floats into the air.

source.name: USGS Water Science School: Evaporation and the water cycle

text: A big, puffy cloud can weigh about as much as a hundred elephants. It floats because its tiny droplets are spread out over a huge space.
Scientists say it is very unlikely that two snowflakes are ever exactly alike. Each one takes its own path through the sky as it grows.

source.name: Mental Floss: Are no two snowflakes alike?

text: Raindrops are not really shaped like teardrops. Small ones are round, and bigger ones flatten out on the bottom like a bun as they fall.

source.name: USGS Water Science School: Raindrops are different shapes

text: You can tell how far away a storm is by timing the seconds between lightning and thunder. Every five seconds is about one mile.
Rainbows are really full circles. From the ground we usually see only an arc, but people in airplanes can sometimes see the whole ring.
Mawsynram in India is one of the rainiest places on Earth. It gets more rain in a year than many cities get in ten years.

source.name: Universe Today: Wettest place on Earth

text: The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth. Some places there have gone years without any rain.
Every day, weather balloons are sent up from hundreds of places around the world. They carry instruments high into the sky to measure the air.
A ring around the Moon is called a halo. It forms when moonlight passes through tiny ice crystals in thin, high clouds.

source.name: EarthSky: What makes a halo around the Moon

text: Sun dogs are bright spots of light that sometimes appear on each side of the Sun. Like halos, they are made by ice crystals in the sky.
Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth. Even in summer, much of it stays far below freezing.

source.name: NASA SVS: Coldest place on Earth

text: Lake effect snow happens when cold wind blows across a warmer lake. The wind picks up moisture and drops heavy snow on the land beyond it.

source.name: NOAA SciJinks: What is lake effect snow?

text: An octopus has three hearts. Its body is soft, with no bones at all.

source.name: Smithsonian Magazine: Ten wild facts about octopuses

text: Sea otters sometimes hold paws while they float and rest, so they do not drift apart.

source.name: Discover: Sea otters hold hands while sleeping

text: The blue whale is the biggest animal on Earth. It can be about as long as a basketball court.

source.name: Dolphin Safari: How big is a blue whale?

text: Starfish are not really fish, so scientists call them sea stars. Many of them have five arms.

source.name: NOAA Ocean Service: Sea star, not a fish

text: Seahorses swim standing up. They hold on to sea grass with their curly tails.
Clownfish live among the stinging arms of sea anemones. A special coat on their skin keeps them from getting stung.
Most of the ocean is very deep and dark. Some fish down there make their own light.
Dolphins rest one half of their brain at a time. That way they can keep swimming and breathing.

source.name: Smithsonian Magazine: Dolphins sleep with half their brain

text: The ocean is salty because rivers carry tiny bits of salt from rocks into the sea.

source.name: WHOI: What makes the ocean salty?

text: Sea turtles can swim across whole oceans. Many come back to the same beach where they hatched.

source.name: Olive Ridley Project: How sea turtles return to the same beach

text: Crabs walk sideways because of the way their legs bend.

source.name: UT Marine Science Institute: Why crabs scuttle sideways

text: Whales breathe air through blowholes on the top of their heads.
Sea stars have a tiny eye at the tip of each arm. The eyes can tell light from dark.
The Pacific is the largest ocean. It is so big that all of the land on Earth could fit inside it.
The Great Barrier Reef off Australia is the largest structure on Earth built by living things. Astronauts can see it from space.

source.name: NASA Earth Observatory: Great Barrier Reef

text: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known part of the ocean. If Mount Everest were placed inside it, the peak would still be more than a mile under water.
An octopus can change both the color and the texture of its skin in a blink. This helps it blend in with rocks and coral.
Humpback whales sing long songs made of moans, cries, and squeaks. Their songs can travel for many miles through the water.

source.name: UT Marine Science Institute: The migration of whale songs

text: About half of the oxygen we breathe is made in the ocean, by tiny floating living things called plankton.

source.name: NOAA Ocean Service: How much oxygen comes from the ocean?

text: Coral may look like rock or plants, but each coral is made of many tiny animals called polyps.

source.name: NOAA Ocean Exploration: Corals are animals

text: Sea otters have the thickest fur of any animal. A single square inch of their fur can hold up to a million hairs.

source.name: NOAA Ocean Today: Sea otter anatomy

text: Most ocean waves are made by wind blowing across the water. The longer and harder the wind blows, the bigger the waves become.
The long tusk of a narwhal is really a tooth. It grows in a spiral and can be longer than a grown person is tall.
The longest mountain range on Earth is under the sea. It runs along the middle of the ocean floor, around the whole planet.
Emperor penguins dive deeper than any other bird. They can swim down more than a quarter of a mile to find food.

source.name: Australian Antarctic Division: Emperor penguin dive depth
